title: BRICS Summit 2026: Full Itinerary, Timings and What to Watch in New Delhi
excerpt: Leaders of the expanded 11-member bloc converge on Bharat Mandapam on September 12–13, with the BRICS Business Forum opening today and traffic restrictions across central Delhi.
body:
• The 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit takes place at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on September 12–13, under India's chairship theme "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability."
  • Saturday is members-only: a closed session on inclusive global governance, a "Bharat Innovates" exhibition, the family photo, a joint tree plantation and a gala dinner hosted by Prime Minister Modi.
  • Sunday opens to partner countries and outreach invitees — including Belarus, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Thailand and UN chief António Guterres — before the open plenary session.
  • Delhi Police will regulate traffic on more than 35 roads from September 11–13, with around 30,000 security personnel deployed across the capital.

New Delhi is decked out in posters and illuminated installations. Motorcades are rehearsing their routes. And over the next three days, the capital hosts one of the largest diplomatic gatherings it has ever staged: the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit, on September 12–13 at Bharat Mandapam in Pragati Maidan.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi said this week that India is fully prepared to host the two-day summit, where Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping will join leaders of the expanded 11-member bloc to deliberate on global issues and ways to strengthen cooperation.

For a summit that will be defined as much by who stands next to whom as by what gets signed, the schedule is unusually choreographed. Here is the full itinerary, the guests to watch, and what is at stake.

Saturday, September 12: members day

The first day belongs to the full members of BRICS. Leaders arrive at Level 2 of Bharat Mandapam at 2 PM, and by 2:35 PM they are inside the Summit Hall for a closed session on "Inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism" — the phrase that has anchored India's entire chairship.

At 4:25 PM, the leaders move to Hall 14 to witness the "Bharat Innovates" exhibition, a showcase of Indian innovation that Delhi has made a fixture of major summits it hosts. The 5:05 PM family photo follows on the outside lawns — the image that will travel the world — and at 5:10 PM, a joint tree plantation on the same lawns. The day closes at 7:30 PM with a gala dinner hosted by the Prime Minister on Level 3 of Bharat Mandapam.

The closed session matters most. With the United States and Iran edging toward escalation — crude has already crossed $100 a barrel this week — the members-only format gives leaders room to negotiate a joint statement without the cameras. Any language on energy security, the Iran conflict and reform of global institutions will have been haggled over by Sherpas in the months of preparatory meetings and will be finalised here.

Sunday, September 13: the expanded circle

Day two opens the summit to the wider BRICS ecosystem. Leaders of partner countries and outreach invitees arrive at 9:55 AM. The family photo is at 10:35 AM, followed at 10:50 AM by the open plenary session — "Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth" — in the Summit Hall. That session is expected to produce the summit's public declaration.

The guest list beyond the 11 members is itself a statement. Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko, Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul are among those attending, and UN Secretary-General António Guterres is likely to take part. India has used its chairship to position BRICS as a platform with ambitions well beyond its formal membership.

"India is fully prepared to host the 18th BRICS Summit."

— Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on the summit preparations

The headline meetings to watch

The ceremonial schedule is only half the story. Modi is expected to hold bilateral meetings on the sidelines, and two stand out.

Putin's attendance is his second visit to India in under a year, following the annual bilateral summit in New Delhi in December 2025. Modi renewed the invitation in person when the two leaders met at the SCO summit in Bishkek on August 31. With Russia supplying a large share of India's oil and defence imports under Western pressure, every Modi–Putin encounter is scrutinised for what it signals about India's strategic autonomy.

Xi Jinping's expected presence carries even more weight. If the Chinese leader attends, it will be his first trip to India since the informal summit with Modi in Mamallapuram in 2019 — a gap defined by the Galwan clash, military standoffs and a slow, grinding normalisation. A Modi–Xi bilateral on the sidelines is widely anticipated, and officials have noted that the Chinese delegation could run to around 400 officials, roughly double its 2019 contingent.

What's on the agenda

Under India's chairship, more than 350 BRICS meetings and high-level engagements have already been held across 25 cities, spanning three pillars: political and security cooperation, economic and financial cooperation, and cultural and people-to-people exchanges.

At the leaders' level, the agenda is concrete: resilient global supply chains, cross-border payment integration, expanded use of national currencies, MSME development, digital trade and artificial intelligence. India has been pushing integration of member countries' central bank digital currencies to make international transactions faster — a proposal with real technical and political hurdles. Food and energy security, health, disaster resilience and technology cooperation round out the list.

The run-up to the summit also carries its own programme. The BRICS Business Forum takes place today, September 11, at the same venue, alongside a session of the Women's Business Alliance — the two tracks where the summit's commercial ambitions get a first airing.

Getting around Delhi

For residents, the summit means disruption. Delhi Traffic Police has finalised a detailed traffic management plan covering more than 35 roads, primarily in central and south Delhi, with temporary stoppages during VIP motorcades. Additional CP (Traffic) Dinesh Kumar Gupta told ANI the arrangements cover September 11, 12 and 13 — delegates and security teams began moving into position today.

Around 30,000 security personnel are being deployed, and authorities have undertaken road repairs and beautification along the leaders' routes. Commuters should expect controlled and diverted traffic across the central corridor through Sunday evening.

Why it matters for the diaspora

BRICS summits rarely produce announcements that change an NRI's week. But the plumbing they negotiate — cross-border payments, national-currency settlement, digital trade frameworks — is the infrastructure that determines how cheap and fast it is to send money home, and how competitive Indian exporters are in world markets.

India's fourth BRICS chairship, twenty years after the bloc's founding, is also a bid to cement New Delhi as a rule-maker rather than a rule-taker in the global economy. Whether that ambition survives the summit's fault lines — an Iran in conflict with the US, a Russia under sanctions, and a China recalibrating its India policy — will be visible in the declaration that emerges on Sunday.

nri_angle: Summit decisions on cross-border payments, national-currency settlement and digital trade set the infrastructure for cheaper remittances and more competitive Indian exporters — and mark India's bid to be a global-economic rule-maker.
